claims.text: Adding a fine, uniformly dispersed population of Y2O3 nanoparticles to MoNbTaW will enhance yield strength at 800–1200 °C relative to conventionally processed MoNbTaW without nanoparticles.
Adding a fine, uniformly dispersed population of Y2O3 nanoparticles to MoNbTaW will enhance high-temperature creep resistance relative to conventionally processed MoNbTaW without nanoparticles.
The Y2O3-reinforced MoNbTaW alloy will maintain improved mechanical performance under irradiation.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering can incorporate a fine, uniform dispersion of Y2O3 nanoparticles into MoNbTaW.
Advanced milling and in situ monitoring protocols will help ensure uniform nanoparticle distribution.
The intervention will produce evenly distributed, sub-micron Y2O3 nanoparticles.
Y2O3 nanoparticles act as stable obstacles to dislocation movement.
Y2O3 nanoparticles impede the migration of radiation-induced defects.
Y2O3 nanoparticles serve as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
Defect-sink activity delays the accumulation of irradiation damage.
The nanoparticle dispersion inhibits high-temperature coarsening.
Dislocation pinning and defect-sink activity increase yield strength and creep resistance while maintaining phase stability under extreme conditions.
The nanoparticle dispersion will reduce irradiation-induced defect accumulation relative to the baseline alloy.
Mechanical enhancement depends on the nanoparticles remaining uniformly distributed without agglomeration.
Excessive nanoparticle volume fractions or poor dispersion could cause embrittlement or localized stress concentrations.
